title: Priorat
description: Steep slate slopes in Catalonia where old Garnacha and Cariñena make powerful, mineral reds.
L: Priorat lies in Catalonia, about 100 km south-west of Barcelona, in rugged hills surrounded by the Montsant mountains. Vineyards climb steep terraces and slopes from 100 to 750 m. It's small, about 2,000 hectares. The climate is Mediterranean but with continental influence: hot, dry summers, cold winters and very little rain.

Priorat's signature soil is llicorella, a dark slate and quartz that glitters in the sun. It's poor, holds little water and forces roots to dig deep, sometimes 15 metres or more. Yields are tiny, often under 1 kg per vine on old vines. The result is concentrated wine with a mineral, sometimes graphite edge.
Dark slate, deep roots, tiny yields
A dark slate and quartz soil

Carthusian monks founded the Scala Dei monastery here in the 12th century, which gave Priorat its name, priory. After phylloxera, the region emptied. In 1989, a group of five producers, including René Barbier, Álvaro Palacios and Carles Pastrana, made wines that stunned critics. Priorat became Spain's second DOCa in 2000, called DOQ in Catalan.
Priorat is named after a medieval priory.
Yes, the Carthusian priory of Scala Dei.
Priorat is steep, dry and small, in Catalonia
Llicorella slate forces deep roots and tiny yields
A 1989 revival led to DOQ status in 2000
Explain the role of old vines

Garnacha and Cariñena, Carignan, are Priorat's traditional grapes, many from old bush vines over 50 or 80 years old. Garnacha gives ripe red fruit, spice and warmth; Cariñena gives acidity, colour and structure. Together, on llicorella, they make powerful, dark, mineral reds, often 14.5 to 15.5% alcohol.

The 1989 pioneers also planted Cabernet Sauvignon, Syrah and Merlot, adding structure and colour to blends. Today many producers focus on the native grapes, especially old Garnacha and Cariñena, and on single vineyards. Whites, from Garnacha Blanca and Macabeo, are rare.
Match each grape to its role.
Old natives lead; international grapes support.
Neighbouring Montsant, which surrounds Priorat, makes similar Garnacha and Cariñena blends at lower prices, on more varied soils.
What do old vines give Priorat's wines?
Old vines on llicorella give very low yields and concentration.
Garnacha and Cariñena are Priorat's traditional grapes
Old bush vines give concentrated, mineral wines
Reading Priorat and eating with it

Labels show DOQ Priorat or DOCa Priorat. Since 2009, Priorat has a place-based classification: Vi de Vila, village wine, from one of 12 villages, like Gratallops or Porrera; Vinya Classificada, classified vineyard; and Gran Vinya Classificada, the top level. It was among the first in Spain to classify by place.
Vi de Vila to Gran Vinya Classificada

Priorat's power suits rich, savoury food: grilled lamb, wild boar, beef stews, Catalan dishes like duck with pears, and aged cheese. Serve at 16 to 18 degrees, decanted. Good Priorat ages 10 to 20 years, softening its alcohol and tannin into dried fruit and earth.
What is Vi de Vila in Priorat?
A village wine from one of 12 villages
Decant young Priorat for an hour or two. Its high alcohol and concentration open up with air.
